sentences.text: Pteraspis was an extinct genus of jawless fish belonging to the heterostracan group.
This creature possessed protective armor plating on its front body, a feature shared with other heterostracan fish.
It featured two wing-like protrusions over its gills and a single protrusion on its back, both derived from armored plates.
The largest recorded specimens of Pteraspis reached an estimated length of 27 cm.
Stiff spines running along its back likely served as protection against predators.
The genus Pteraspis was described by Kner in 1847, with Kner serving as the authority for the name.
Pteraspis likely fed on shoals of plankton just beneath the ocean surface, specifically on shallow banks below the water.
Its horn-shaped rostrum and wing-like protrusions made the animal a highly aerodynamic form, suggesting good swimming ability.
The type species for the genus Pteraspis is Cephalaspis rostrata.
Known species of Pteraspis include P. rostrata, P. dunensis, and P. crouchi.
Pteraspis lived from 419.62 to 387.95 million years ago during the Lochkovian to Eifelian stages.
It inhabited regions now known as the Americas and Europe.
Fossil records of Pteraspis are found in both marine and freshwater environments.
